name: Cryptocurrency
summary: Cryptocurrency addresses, transactions, tokens and non-custodial services on every chain, identified by network as well as value: the same string on Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash, or on Ethereum and BSC, is two nodes. Public identifiers only.
description:
Reach for it to follow funds on-chain: from an address through its transactions and tokens to the services and exchanges it touches. One set of types covers every chain and `network` says which, because the same string is a different account elsewhere: a `1…` address on Bitcoin and on Bitcoin Cash, or one `0x…` address on Ethereum and on BSC, hold different funds and are separate nodes.

- **Letter case.** Hex, bech32, CashAddr and TON raw values match whatever their case, so an EIP-55 checksummed address and its lower-case form are one node. Base58 values (legacy Bitcoin, TRON, Solana, Monero, XRPL) are compared exactly.
- **Network not established.** `evm` is a `0x…` address whose chain is not known yet, `unknown` any other address whose network neither the source nor the format settles. Each stays its own node and links to the node on an established network with `same address on`, which for a contract does not mean the same owner.
- **Exchanges and other custodians** (OTC desks, custodial wallets, payment processors that hold funds) are the Financial pack's `financial.exchange`; `crypto_service` is for services that do not hold customer funds.
- **Amounts** are decimal strings in the network's native unit: full precision, but they do not sort as numbers.
- **Link labels:** `sent to`, `deployed`, `input to`, `output to`, `token contract`, `attributed to`, `same address on`, `listed address`, `accepts payment to`, `same as`.
- **CAIP-2 chain ids:** bitcoin `bip122:000000000019d6689c085ae165831e93`, bitcoin_cash `bip122:000000000000000000651ef99cb9fcbe`, litecoin `bip122:12a765e31ffd4059bada1e25190f6e98`, dogecoin `bip122:1a91e3dace36e2be3bf030a65679fe82`; the EVM chains `eip155:` plus their chain id (ethereum 1, ethereum_classic 61, bsc 56, polygon 137, arbitrum 42161, optimism 10, base 8453, avalanche_c 43114); tron `tron:728126428`, solana `solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp`, xrpl `xrpl:0`, ton `tvm:-239`; drafts bitcoin_sv `bsv:mainnet`, monero `monero:418015bb9ae982a1975da7d79277c270`, bnb_beacon `cosmos:Binance-Chain-Tigris`; cardano proposed as `cardano:1-764824073`. bitcoin_gold, dash, zcash and verge have none registered; `evm` and `unknown` none by definition.

**Source:** https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/typepack-cryptocurrency (`typepacks/cryptocurrency.json`). Licence: Apache-2.0.

types.name: crypto_address
types.description: A public address on one network. The same string on another network is another node, and `evm` or `unknown` holds an address whose network is not established yet.

network.description: The network the address is on. `evm`: a 0x address whose chain is not established; `unknown`: neither the source nor the format settles it.

address.description: The address in its canonical form. Hex, bech32, CashAddr and TON raw values match whatever their letter case; Base58 is compared exactly.

memo.description: A value given together with the address that selects the recipient behind it, such as an XRPL destination tag. Empty on most networks.

address_kind.description: What the address is: an externally owned account or a contract, a Bitcoin-family script type, a token account.

tx_count.description: Number of transactions involving the address.

balance.description: Balance as a decimal string in the network's native unit (BTC, ETH, TRX, …).

balance_source.description: Where the balance was read. Services count some outputs differently, so two sources can disagree.

activated_at.description: When the address was activated or first funded (TRON activation, XRPL account creation, first incoming transfer).

first_funder.description: The address that sent the first funds.

first_funding_tx.description: Hash of the first funding transaction.

deployer.description: For a contract, the address that deployed it.

deployment_tx.description: For a contract, the hash of its deployment transaction.

public_label.description: A public label or tag, e.g. an exchange's hot wallet.

frozen_by_issuer.description: The stablecoin whose issuer has frozen this address, e.g. "USDT (Tether)".

sanctions_programs.description: Sanctions programmes the listing names, one entry each (e.g. CYBER2, DPRK3).

sanctions_as_of.description: Date of the list the sanctions fields come from.

history_examined.description: Transactions read when the history was examined.

history_complete.description: Whether the whole history was read; false when a run stopped at its limit.

types.name: crypto_transaction
types.description: One on-chain transaction. Chains that forked share their earlier history, so the same txid can exist on Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash, and `network` says which one this is.

network.description: The network the transaction is on.

tx_hash.description: Transaction hash or id. A 64-hex hash matches with or without 0x and in either case; other forms, such as a Solana signature, are compared exactly.

block_height.description: Height of the block that includes it.

fee.description: Fee paid, as a decimal string in the network's native unit.

types.name: crypto_token
types.description: A token on one network: an ERC-20 or NFT contract, a TRC-20, an SPL mint, a jetton, an XRPL issued currency. Its contract is also a Crypto Address, linked to this node by `token contract`. Native assets (BTC, ETH, TRX) have no token node.

network.description: The network the token is on.

contract_address.description: The token's contract address; for Solana the mint, for XRPL currency.issuer.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol, as the contract states it.

name.description: Token name, as the contract states it.

decimals.description: Decimal places of the token's unit.

issuer.description: Who issues the token, e.g. Tether.

types.name: crypto_service
types.description: A service that moves funds without holding them for customers: a mixer, bridge, gambling site, merchant or DeFi protocol. An exchange, OTC desk, custodial wallet or payment processor that holds funds is a financial.exchange.

service_type.description: What kind of service it is.

attribution_source.description: Where the identification of the service comes from.
